interface.signature: def floodFill(image: List[List[int]], sr: int, sc: int, newColor: int) -> List[List[int]]:

preconditions.expression: all(isinstance(row, list) and all(isinstance(pixel, int) for pixel in row) for row in image)
preconditions.description: The input `image` is a 2-D list of integers, where each integer represents a pixel value.

preconditions.expression: len(image) >= 1 and all(len(row) >= 1 for row in image)
preconditions.description: The `image` is non-empty, with each row having at least one pixel.
The starting coordinates `(sr, sc)` are valid indices within the `image` bounds.
The `newColor` is a valid pixel value within the allowed range.

postconditions.expression: all(row == orig_row for row, orig_row in zip(return_value, image)) or any(pixel != orig_pixel for pixel, orig_pixel in zip(row, orig_row) for row, orig_row in zip(return_value, image))
postconditions.description: The returned `image` is either identical to the input (if no pixels were changed) or at least one pixel value differs from the original.

postconditions.expression: all(return_value[r][c] == newColor if (r == sr and c == sc) or (r != sr or c != sc and return_value[r][c] == newColor and (image[r][c] == image[sr][sc])) else return_value[r][c] == image[r][c] for r in range(len(return_value)) for c in range(len(return_value[r])))
postconditions.description: For every pixel `(r, c)` in the returned image, if it is part of the connected region (4-directionally) of the original starting pixel color, it is set to `newColor`; otherwise, it retains its original value.

postconditions.expression: all(return_value[r][c] == image[r][c] or return_value[r][c] == newColor for r in range(len(return_value)) for c in range(len(return_value[r])))
postconditions.description: Every pixel in the returned image is either unchanged from the original or set to `newColor`.
